METHOD / DENOMINATORS
- Enumerated all 1,799 records across all 16 kinds: action 10, ancestry 13, background 1, class 12, condition 15, creature 317, equipment 219, feat 1, feature 179, hazard 25, magic-item 240, rule 325, spell 319, stat-block 2, subclass 12, table 109. - Independently extracted the pinned PDF with pdftotext -raw and -layout to /tmp/l1-srd-raw.txt and /tmp/l1-srd-layout.txt. Compared producer-declared source-prose with cited PDF pages, using normalized nonoverlapping eight-word windows for 3,550 string fields of at least eight words across 1,605 records, then a separate short-string/adjacent-page sibling sweep. Removing PDF footers and ignoring layout/hyphen punctuation reduced long-field suspects from 237 to 69; suspects were triaged, not automatically promoted. Table removal, interleaved columns, typographic apostrophes, and correct nested option.source citations explain many lexical mismatches.
- Independently checked 799 anchors across all 344 existing fieldLocators: spell names on each cited spell-list page and capacity/primary-ability values on their cited pages. No mismatched anchor found. This does not independently reconstruct spell class membership or prove that absent fieldLocators should be absent.
- Checked 2,536 creature, 15 inline-stat-block, and 392 equipment scalar anchors against cited PDF pages (AC, HP/formula, ability-score/modifier, printed cost/weight/damage where available); no absent scalar anchor found. Page-level occurrence alone does not prove correct row/record ownership.
- Enumerated 2,267 mechanics-bearing containers for an independent explicit save DC/ability-pair and attack-bonus source-text screen; no impossible numeric pair found. Separately inspected selected source branches/options/resources and semantic subjects, including all 45 rollModifier effects across the 31 spells carrying that kind, and screened all 514 creature/stat-block attack objects for same-sentence save-governed damage. The latter yielded 14 affected entries in 13 records (F5).
- Reproduction scripts: /tmp/l1-prose-scan.py, /tmp/l1-prose-scan-v2.py, /tmp/l1-typed-scan.py, /tmp/l1-source-scalars.py, and /tmp/l1-findings.py. FINDINGS FOLLOW IN SUBSEQUENT NOTES. All five findings are retained source/provenance contradictions. None depends on a universal completeness or deterministic execution claim.
L1-F1 — BLOCKER — retained prose/cells cite incomplete record locators
Bar violated: 2 (truthful provenance); source traceability under bar 1. RECURRENCE: locator-completeness / indep:008; related source-provenance-fields / sol:CAP-010. The existing ledger-based test only compares the ledger's assigned pages; independent source comparison finds content that the ledger never assigns to these records. For example, the ledger contains no targetKey entry at all for table:bag-of-beans or table:food-drink-and-lodging, so that comparison cannot protect their continuations.

Concrete candidate witnesses (JSON pointers are relative to record.data; none has an overriding fieldLocator):
1. ancestry:dragonborn, provenance.locator='p. 5', /traits/7/text: 'You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.' This is on SRD p. 6, not p. 5. /traits/6/text also continues onto p. 6 (damage scaling and rest reset), and /traits/8/text is on p. 6.
2. ancestry:hill-dwarf, locator='p. 4', /traits/1/text begins 'Dwarves mature at the same rate as humans' on p. 3. Flattened parent traits include the p. 3 Constitution increase, speed, combat training, resilience, Stonecunning, and language text; the parent source page is absent from this record's provenance.
3. ancestry:lightfoot-halfling, locator='p. 5', /traits/5/text begins 'When you roll a 1 on the d20' on p. 4, including Lucky's reroll rule. Other inherited p. 4 traits are likewise present but uncited.
4. table:bag-of-beans, locator='p. 209', /rows/10/1 begins 'A pyramid with a 60-foot-square base bursts upward.' This and the final beanstalk row are on p. 210; the eggs row also crosses the page boundary.
5. table:celtic-deities, locator='p. 360', /rows/9/0='Math Mathonwy, god of magic' is on p. 361. The last five deity rows are there, through Silvanus.
6. table:gray-bag-of-tricks, locator='p. 210', /rows/6/1='Dire wolf' and /rows/7/1='Giant elk' are on p. 211. The printed p. 210 table stops at row 6 (Giant badger).
7. table:half-dragon-damage-resistance, locator='p. 320', /rows/2/0='Brass, gold, or red' is on p. 321. The green and silver/white rows also continue there.
8. table:lifestyle-expenses, locator='p. 72', /rows/6/1='10 gp minimum' is on p. 73. The printed p. 72 table stops after Squalid.
9. table:food-drink-and-lodging, locator='p. 73', /rows/2/0='Banquet (per person)' is on p. 74; p. 73 only carries the Ale rows. Almost the whole retained table therefore has no correct record-level page citation.
10. magic-item:bag-of-tricks, locator='p. 210', carries gray/rust/tan /variants text with no own variant source or field locator; the gray final rows and complete Rust/Tan tables are printed on p. 211. The separate Rust/Tan table records correctly cite p. 211, but the variant fields copied into the parent are not assigned that provenance.

Reproducer: python3 /tmp/l1-findings.py, L1-F1 section. The first nine assertions independently establish both presence on the actual page and absence from the record's cited page(s). Parent/subrace and table references make the correct sources recoverable elsewhere, but do not make these retained fields' own page attribution complete. In contrast, Champion Additional Fighting Style options explicitly carry their own truthful 'SRD 5.1 p. 24' source fields; that lexical flag was rejected as a finding.

Consequence/boundary: the pack presents correct source content under incomplete authoritative citations. Source fidelity/provenance is required independently of a runtime consumer or capability selection. This is a provenance failure, not a demand for more mechanics.
Suggested owner/fix: provenance/source-accounting compiler owner, successor to eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2. Carry actual inherited/continued source spans into record locators or truthful field-level locators; correct the accounting ownership so the existing gate has an independent denominator for emitted table and flattened ancestry content. Do not widen arbitrary locators just to satisfy a ledger mismatch. Regenerate through the compiler.
Permanent evidence: generalized continuation/inheritance provenance invariant, retaining the exact source-backed witnesses above until broader evidence demonstrably preserves them. Modest text/page assertions suffice; no new expensive global proof system is required.

L1-F2 — BLOCKER — compiler-composed displays still classified as verbatim source authority
Bar violated: 2 and 7. RECURRENCE: source-authority-fable-f5 / fable:F5, source-authority-fable-f7 / fable:F7, and the composed-text distinction in source-authority-opus-f19 / opus:F-19.

Operative contract: packages/core/src/rules/fieldProvenance.ts:23 defines source-prose as 'literal text reproduced from the source' and the only class a consumer may present as verbatim authority. Generated field-provenance.json instead classifies the following constructed strings as source-prose, with reasons asserting literal/quoted/verbatim text:
- feature:draconic-bloodline:dragon-ancestor /choices/0/options/*/text. Example: 'Dragon: Black; Damage Type: Acid'. SRD p. 44 prints the column headers 'Dragon' and 'Damage Type', then the row 'Black Acid'; it does not print that labeled sentence. deriveFeatureChoices.ts:1812 explicitly constructs it with header/cell interpolation and semicolons. All ten options share the false verbatim classification.
- feature:circle-of-the-land:circle-spells /choices/0/options/*/text. Example starts 'Druid Level 3rd: hold person, spike growth; Druid Level 5th: sleet storm, slow'. SRD p. 22 prints separate level/spell rows under a single header, not repeated 'Druid Level' prose. All seven land options are composed displays.
- magic-item:elemental-gem /variants/*/text, e.g. 'Summoned elemental: Air elemental.' SRD p. 220 prints 'Gem / Summoned Elemental' as table headings and 'Blue sapphire / Air elemental' as a row. parseMagicItems.ts:433 constructs the sentence. All four variants are affected.
- magic-item:horn-of-valhalla /variants/*/text, e.g. 'Berserkers Summoned: 2d4 + 2. Requirement: None.' The p. 226 source prints table cells under separate headings, not that sentence. parseMagicItems.ts:366 constructs it. All four variants are affected.
- magic-item:bag-of-tricks /variants/*/text, e.g. 'd8 creatures: 1 Weasel; 2 Giant rat; ...'. SRD pp. 210-211 have separate numbered Creature tables; parseMagicItems.ts:528 constructs the display. All three variants are affected.
- table:travel-pace /columns/1..3: 'Distance per Minute', 'Distance per Hour', 'Distance per Day'. SRD p. 84 prints the spanning header 'Distance Traveled per . . .' and subheaders 'Minute', 'Hour', 'Day'. parseTables.ts:1273-1275 supplies the expanded labels; the declaration still calls them quoted printed column labels.
- table:food-drink-and-lodging /rows strings, e.g. 'Inn stay, squalid (per day)'. SRD p. 74 prints the group header 'Inn stay (per day)' and row label 'Squalid' separately. parseTables.ts:904 and :922 document the compiler's folding, but /rows is declared verbatim source-prose.
- table:services /rows, e.g. 'Coach cab, within a city'. SRD p. 74 prints the group header 'Coach cab' and row 'Within a city' separately. The folded display inherits the same false /rows classification.

This is at least eight records spanning feature, magic-item, and table. Reproducer: python3 /tmp/l1-findings.py, L1-F2 section. Producer declarations causing the misclassification: fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts:833-836 (feature option bodies), namedEntry magic-item variants, and :1182-1196 (table columns/rows). The rows/headers/choices contain legitimate source-derived facts; the defect is their retained assertion of verbatim authority, not the existence of structured or composed representations.

Consequence/boundary: compiler text can be presented as source quotation under the SRD's authoritative provenance/license. Prior repairs of background labels and Scrying headers did not cover sibling producer shapes.
Suggested owner/fix: source-authority/field-provenance owner, successor to eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1. Truthfully classify constructed displays as source-derived/compiler-projection as appropriate, or retain literal source fields separately. Preserve accurate attribution for actual source content; do not demote or remove genuine verbatim passages to hide the problem.
Permanent evidence: generalized producer-to-provenance classification checks for constructed option/variant/table displays, with the concrete p. 22/44/74/84/220/226 witnesses retained until equivalently protected. A source-prose declaration's presence/schema coverage alone is insufficient evidence of its truth.
L1-F3 — BLOCKER — spell rollModifier assigns the benefit to the wrong actor
Bar violated: 1 (source fidelity of retained typed content). RECURRENCE: spell-mechanics-depth / sol:CAP-003. Its current narrowed disposition specifically retains the obligation that emitted projections agree with source; no complete spell-mechanics claim is needed.

Concrete evidence in records.json:
- spell:guiding-bolt /mechanics/effects/0 = {kind:'rollModifier', subject:'target', mode:'advantage', scope:'attack-rolls'}. SRD pp. 151-152: 'the next attack roll made against this target before the end of your next turn has advantage'. The advantage belongs to the next attacker against the target, not the illuminated target's own attack rolls. The projection also discards the next-attack scope.
- spell:irresistible-dance /mechanics/effects/0 = {kind:'rollModifier', subject:'target', mode:'advantage', scope:'attack rolls against it'}. SRD p. 158: 'While the target is affected by this spell, other creatures have advantage on attack rolls against it.' The structured subject is the dancing target, whereas the source explicitly names other creatures. The preceding source sentence gives the dancer disadvantage on its own attacks.
- spell:holy-aura /mechanics/effects/0 = {kind:'rollModifier', subject:'caster', mode:'advantage', scope:'all saving throws, and other creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against them until the spell ends'}. SRD p. 155 says 'Creatures of your choice in that radius when you cast this spell ... have advantage on all saving throws'. The eligible recipients are the chosen creatures in the radius; the caster need not be selected. The parser incorrectly binds to embedded 'you' in 'when you cast this spell'.

Mechanism: mechanicsProjections.ts:1047-1060 and :1363-1374 choose a nearest recognized noun/pronoun, not the grammatical subject of the modifier. 'Other creatures' and the 'attack roll made against this target' phrase are not represented by that subject matcher, and the enclosing sentence's 'you' can steal the subject. The output's structured subject is a positive incorrect fact, not merely missing structure. Reproducer: python3 /tmp/l1-findings.py, L1-F3.
Sibling analysis: inspected all 45 rollModifier projections across all 31 spell records carrying that effect. Additional controls included the three Dominate spells, Blur, Hunter's Mark, Shocking Grasp, Haste, and Resurrection. Resurrection's caster disadvantage is supported by its separate more-than-one-year-dead drawback and is not a wrong-subject finding. Conditions/timing omitted elsewhere were not automatically promoted as source errors.
Suggested owner/fix: spell compiler projection owner, successor to eshyra-o9bd.19.4.1. Preserve the real recipient and scope with bounded grammar/curation, or omit the misleading projection while retaining authoritative prose for DM adjudication. Do not default an unrecognized grammatical subject to target/caster.
Permanent evidence: generalized subject/recipient invariant over retained roll modifiers, with exact PDF-backed cases for object-of-preposition, embedded-caster-clause, and explicit-other-creatures forms plus correct-neighbor controls. This is proportionate to the retained source claim; a live model run is unnecessary to demonstrate the contradiction.

L1-F4 — BLOCKER — Empty Body falsely grants force resistance
Bar violated: 1 (source fidelity). RECURRENCE: class-feature-completeness / indep:003, under its narrowed surviving obligation that emitted structured feature data remain source-faithful.

Concrete evidence: feature:monk:empty-body /mechanics/effects/0 is {kind:'damageResistance', types:'all'}. SRD p. 28, Empty Body: 'During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage.' The retained field grants force resistance; no exception field is present. The correct source sentence remains in /description, making this a direct contradiction between the typed assertion and its own source.
Mechanism: mechanicsProjections.ts:5376-5377 matches the prefix /resistance to all damage/ and emits types:'all' without admitting or rejecting the following exception. Reproducer: python3 /tmp/l1-findings.py, L1-F4.
Sibling analysis: searched the complete corpus for all-damage resistance and exception-bearing resistance. Checked Petrified (p. 359), Ioun Stone (p. 227), Warding Bond (p. 191), Hallow (p. 152), and Armor of Invulnerability (p. 208). Petrified's all-damage claim is source-backed; the armor's all-damage resistance carries its explicit magical-damage exclusion; absent Hallow/Warding Bond resistance projections were not treated as defects. Empty Body is the concrete bad positive found in this search.
Suggested owner/fix: feature projection owner, successor to eshyra-o9bd.19.3.2. Preserve the force exception (and applicable duration/activation scope where the representation requires it), or fail closed by omitting the incorrect resistance effect and leaving the text DM-adjudicated. A new deterministic capability is not required.
Permanent evidence: retain the exact p. 28 regression and a generalized negative for exception-bearing input to an all-damage grammar, with an unqualified all-damage positive control. This protects a printed exception at low cost.

L1-F5 — BLOCKER — same-sentence saving-throw damage is emitted as unconditional attack hitDamage
Bar violated: 1 (source fidelity of typed branches). RECURRENCE: creature-statblock-mechanics / sol:CAP-004, whose narrowed disposition retains agreement of emitted attack/damage projections with the printed stat block. Related repaired branch class: half-damage-branches / opus:F-25; the new defect is damage ownership, not simply a missing 'half' flag.

Concrete examples:
- creature:giant-centipede /actions/0/mechanics/attacks/0/hitDamage contains BOTH 1d4+2 piercing and 3d6 poison. SRD p. 374 Bite: 'Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or take 10 (3d6) poison damage.' A successful save takes no poison damage. The retained attack hitDamage nevertheless lists that poison as another ordinary on-hit term, and saves[0] has no damageOnFailure ownership.
- creature:giant-scorpion /actions/2/mechanics/attacks/0/hitDamage contains BOTH 1d10+2 piercing and 4d10 poison. SRD p. 378 Sting: 'the target must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.' The printed branch only changes poison, never the piercing hit damage. Candidate saves[0].damageOnSuccess='half' is present but unattached to a failure-damage list, while poison is also encoded as unconditional hitDamage.
- creature:quasit /actions/0 (p. 273) and both Assassin attacks /actions/1 and /actions/2 (p. 396) repeat the no-damage-on-success and half-poison variants of the same class.

Mechanism: mechanicsProjections.ts:615-686 parses every damage term within the Hit sentence as the hit's damage list, even when a save clause intervenes. :758-805 routes save-owned damage only for attacks with alternatives and only outside the parsed attack sentence. The correctly separated Swarm of Poisonous Snakes projection demonstrates the available distinction: its hitDamage holds piercing only, and its save owns poison via damageOnFailure. Ordinary same-sentence save-bearing attacks have not received the same ownership treatment.

Sibling census: a full query over 514 attack objects finds 14 entries in 13 candidate records with multiple hitDamage terms and a same-Hit-sentence save before damage: Assassin Shortsword and Light Crossbow; Giant Centipede Bite; Giant Poisonous Snake Bite; Giant Scorpion Sting; Giant Spider Bite; Giant Wasp Sting; Giant Wolf Spider Bite; Guardian Naga Bite; Imp Sting; Phase Spider Bite; Purple Worm Tail Stinger; Quasit Claws; Spirit Naga Bite. Source locators and typed values for all 14 are printed by /tmp/l1-findings.py (L1-F5 section), and their prose is present in the independently extracted PDF source. This is a bounded grammar cohort, not a claim that every attack branch is now enumerated.
Controls: Bone Devil, Erinyes, and Ettercap explicitly deal extra poison on hit and use a separate save for the poisoned condition; those poison terms correctly remain hit damage. Balor's Whip likewise deals fire on hit and saves only against being pulled. These were not counted as failures merely for having both damage and a save.

Consequence/boundary: the typed attack list falsely merges damage that is guaranteed by a hit with damage governed by a save, so a consumer cannot use hitDamage as the attack's unconditional damage. This is a retained projection defect; this audit does not claim to have demonstrated an already-executing runtime damage application bug.
Suggested owner/fix: creature attack grammar owner, successor to eshyra-o9bd.19.4.2 / .19.4.3. Distinguish direct on-hit terms from save-governed terms within the sentence, preserve success/failure ownership, or omit unsupported branch projections. Keep unconditional poison controls intact and regenerate.
Permanent evidence: generalized source-backed save-damage routing invariant covering both save-negates and save-halves forms, across the sibling cohort, plus the unconditional-poison/condition-save controls. Retain the exact source-backed examples until equivalent or stronger broader coverage replaces them.
